messages:
lina (Partner Eng): Heads up: BlueArc deployment to MediScale staging failed during init. init container exits immediately, customer blocked on go-live tasks. Need quick architecture triage.

jake (Solutions): can you paste the container logs / events?

lina (Partner Eng): logs:

```
InitContainer "setup-kv" failed: exit code 1
stderr: failed to create socket /var/run/kv/agent.sock: Permission denied
Events:
  Warning  FailedMount  12s  kubelet  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kv-socket": hostPath type check failed: /var/run/kv is not a socket
```

ada (ML Eng): My hunch: SELinux or the AMI's runtime changed hostPath semantics. MediScale uses a locked-down RHEL AMI and a CRI that treats hostPath types strictly.

mike (Infra): On it. Requesting node access and will run `ls -Z /var/run/kv` and `stat -c %F /var/run/kv`.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2031 created. Severity: P2. Assigned: infra-oncall.

nora (SI PM): Looping in BlueArc eng; their marketplace image was built last week. @bluearc-bot can you confirm the image tag and entrypoint behavior?

bluearc-bot: Image pulled: bluearc/agent:v2.1.0 (sha256:deafbeef)
bluearc-bot: Entry-point creates a unix domain socket at /var/run/kv/agent.sock during startup. No container-level privileged ops.

jake (Solutions): If entrypoint expects to create a socket on a hostPath that is a directory, kube will complain if type mismatch occurs. MediScale probably mounted an emptyDir earlier in their cluster but in private deploy it's a hostPath.

lina (Partner Eng): BlueArc claims this used to work in their QA. Possible image variant or a change in our private runtime policy. We need two tracks: fast unblock + long-term compatibility.

mike (Infra): Node findings: `/var/run/kv` exists as a directory owned by root:root, SELinux type `var_run_t`. AVC shows denial: container_t trying to create socker in var_run_t. `getenforce` = Enforcing.

ada (ML Eng): Short-term options:
- Change init to create socket in an ephemeral writable dir (e.g., /tmp) and symlink/move (if allowed)
- Add SELinux policy for container_t -> allow creating socket in var_run_t (needs package & restart)
- Change mount to use hostPath type: Socket (only works if node has socket present)
Running init as privileged would work but customer won't accept.

jake (Solutions): Proposed immediate plan:
1) BlueArc to release v2.1.1 that writes socket to /run/bluearc and avoids assuming hostPath socket.
2) If BlueArc can't ship within 1 hour, we rollback routing to bluearc:v2.0.8 (sha256:abc123) which we validated on MediScale yesterday.
3) Infra to reproduce on a non-prod node with same AMI and test SELinux relabeling steps.

Can we align on that in a 30-min sync?

nora (SI PM): Scheduled triage call: https://cal.com/redwood/23?ts=1732106400. Invite sent to BlueArc, MediScale infra, partner-eng, infra-oncall, solutions.

bluearc-bot: BlueArc engineer reports: quick fix ready — changing socket path and adding graceful fallback. Will deliver a patched image in ~40 minutes.

lina (Partner Eng): Great. Action owners: BlueArc → build/publish v2.1.1 and notify when pushed. Mike → spin a staging node with same RHEL AMI and test the hostPath behavior + try an SELinux permissive test. Ada → verify init code path for race conditions (ensure socket created before dependent containers start). I'll update INC-2031 and post rollback route if needed.

mike (Infra): Will also attach node debug archive to INC-2031 and test with `setenforce 0` on a dev node to reproduce.

jake (Solutions): Reminder: if we switch to a different image via routing policy, update Marketplace onboarding checklist to record required hostPath expectations. @docs FYI.

lina (Partner Eng): Thanks all — will post a short resolution note after the triage call. If BlueArc patch lands earlier we'll coordinate a canary rollout to MediScale staging first. :white_check_mark:
